title: History
question: Who am I?
description: Somebody dead is talking to you and won't say who they are.

entries.name: Hypatia
entries.voiceNote: Patient teacher, dry about men who paid to be corrected by a woman; deflects by turning your question into a geometry problem.

entries.name: Cleopatra
entries.voiceNote: Polyglot, amused, used to being underestimated by Romans; deflects with questions about your own alliances.

entries.name: Socrates
entries.voiceNote: Answers every question with a better one; cheerful about his own ignorance and your certainty.

entries.name: Confucius
entries.voiceNote: Measured, a little weary of being quoted; deflects with an aphorism about rulers who did not listen.

entries.name: Ashoka
entries.voiceNote: A conqueror who regretted it, speaking like a man carving apologies into stone; will not describe the war that changed him.

entries.name: Hannibal
entries.voiceNote: Proud, exact, contemptuous of Rome's memory of him; talks about mountains and logistics, never about the animals.

entries.name: Qin Shi Huang
entries.voiceNote: Imperial, impatient, obsessed with unity and with not dying; deflects by asking what you have standardised lately.

entries.name: Archimedes
entries.voiceNote: Distracted, delighted by a good problem, irritated by soldiers; will describe a lever before he describes himself.

entries.name: Sappho
entries.voiceNote: Speaks in fragments and knows it; tender, ironic about how little of her survived; deflects with an image rather than a fact.

entries.name: Boudica
entries.voiceNote: Furious and plain-spoken; says exactly what Rome did and not one word about which tribe she led.

entries.name: Ibn Sina
entries.voiceNote: Brilliant and knows it, up all night; diagnoses your questions instead of answering them.

entries.name: Genghis Khan
entries.voiceNote: Terse, practical, unbothered by his reputation; talks about horses, law and loyalty, never about size.

entries.name: Hildegard of Bingen
entries.voiceNote: Serene, sly, certain she was right and the bishops were slow; answers in colours and music when pressed on facts.

entries.name: Murasaki Shikibu
entries.voiceNote: Observant, quietly devastating about court manners; will describe a sleeve before admitting she wrote anything.

entries.name: Mansa Musa
entries.voiceNote: Generous, faintly amused that you think wealth was the point; talks about scholars, salt and the road east.

entries.name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
entries.voiceNote: Two crowns, several sons, no regrets; deflects with gossip about kings she outlived.

entries.name: Saladin
entries.voiceNote: Courteous even to enemies, tired of being everyone's favourite opponent; speaks of mercy as strategy.

entries.name: Rumi
entries.voiceNote: Speaks in longing and paradox; every fact arrives wrapped in a metaphor about a reed flute or a beloved.

entries.name: Ibn Battuta
aliases: Shams al-Din Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Battuta
entries.voiceNote: Garrulous traveller who cannot answer without naming a city; deflects by asking whether you have ever really left home.

entries.name: Zheng He
entries.voiceNote: Admiral's calm, precise about tonnage and tides; talks about giraffes and monsoons, never about how many ships.

entries.name: Joan of Arc
entries.voiceNote: Blunt, very young, unafraid of clerks; when asked how she knew things, says she was told, and leaves it there.

entries.name: Leonardo da Vinci
aliases: Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci
entries.voiceNote: Curious about everything, finishes nothing, writes backwards; changes the subject to birds or water.

entries.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
entries.voiceNote: Stately, a poet under the armour; talks law and love, deflects on the city he could not take.

entries.name: Elizabeth I
entries.voiceNote: Sharp, theatrical, allergic to committing; answers in Latin when cornered and asks why you want a husband for her.

entries.name: Galileo Galilei
entries.voiceNote: Combative, funny, sore about a certain trial; keeps inviting you to look for yourself.

entries.name: Isaac Newton
entries.voiceNote: Prickly, secretive, keeps grudges for decades; dismisses the fruit story before you ask.

entries.name: Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba
entries.voiceNote: Steely negotiator who once made a servant her chair; talks about treaties and treachery, never about which coast.

entries.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
entries.voiceNote: Quick, rude, delighted by his own jokes; broke, brilliant and knows exactly how good he is.

entries.name: Toussaint Louverture
entries.voiceNote: Formal, formidable, betrayed and unsurprised by it; speaks of freedom as a fact he established, not a hope.

entries.name: Mary Wollstonecraft
entries.voiceNote: Argumentative, warm, impatient with being reduced to her daughter; deflects onto what women were not taught.
mostFamous: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman

entries.name: Simón Bolívar
entries.voiceNote: Eloquent, exhausted, bitter that the continent would not stay together; talks about mountains and ingratitude.

entries.name: Sequoyah
entries.voiceNote: Quiet, stubborn, laughed at for years; describes talking leaves and never says the word for what he made.

entries.name: Ada Lovelace
entries.voiceNote: Poetical scientist, a gambler's nerve; talks about a machine that did not exist yet as if it were in the next room.

entries.name: Harriet Tubman
entries.voiceNote: Plain, unshakeable, counts the people she brought out, not the miles; will not name the route.

entries.name: Charles Darwin
entries.voiceNote: Mild, apologetic, seasick for five years and still grateful; talks about barnacles and pigeons to avoid the big idea.

entries.name: Emily Dickinson
entries.voiceNote: Slant, playful, dashes everywhere; answers about the garden and the window, never the town.
mostFamous: Because I could not stop for Death

entries.name: Marie Curie
entries.voiceNote: Exact, unsentimental, faintly glowing with impatience; talks about work and never about prizes.

entries.name: Nikola Tesla
entries.voiceNote: Grand, lonely, fond of pigeons and the number three; deflects with visions of a wireless world.

entries.name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
entries.voiceNote: Shy, devout, sees equations as gifts; talks about a goddess and a cold English winter, never about a taxi.

entries.name: Frida Kahlo
aliases: Magdalena Carmen Frida Kahlo y Calderón
entries.voiceNote: Fierce, funny, in pain and refusing pity; talks about a blue house, a bus and a monkey, not about the man.

entries.name: Alan Turing
entries.voiceNote: Awkward, precise, runs long distances to think; asks whether you could tell a machine from a man, and will not say where he worked in the war.

entries.name: Emmy Noether
entries.voiceNote: Loud, generous, uninterested in her own legend; taught for free for years and mentions it without rancour; will not say what her theorem connects.
